He denies fever, chest pain, or hemoptysis.
On physical examination, he appears mildly tachypneic but is hemodynamically stable.
There is decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion over the left lower lung field, with reduced tactile fremitus in the same area.
Chest x-ray reveals a moderate left-sided pleural effusion, occupying nearly one-third of the hemithorax.
The decision is made to perform a diagnostic thoracentesis at the left midaxillary line to determine the nature of the effusion.
To minimize risk of complications, the resident is instructed to insert the needle at the correct intercostal level and position relative to the rib.
